subject: Post-call: FinLytics token volumes & regional pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: token volumes, budget range, next steps

Hi Alicia — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and where we land on next steps so we have clarity before I pull together formal pricing: 

Summary of what I heard
- Product: customer-facing recommendation assistant embedded in analytics UI. Low-latency chat + follow-up generations.
- Usage pattern: ~40k active users in scope for year 1 (pilot -> regional rollouts).
- Interaction profile: average of 2.5 prompts per user per day; median prompt size ~60 tokens; median response ~220 tokens (longer explanations and examples).
- Rough token projection: 40k users * 2.5 interactions/day * (60+220)=280 tokens/interaction -> ~28M tokens/day -> ~840M tokens/month (30-day). Range you called out: 500M–1B tokens/month depending on adoption.

Budget & unit economics
- You mentioned a target unit cost in the neighborhood of $10–15 per 1M tokens (target $/1M: ~$12).
- High-level budget range for the pilot phase you indicated: $8k–$12k/month, scaling to $90k–$120k/month if adoption reaches the upper bound.

Regional / data residency notes
- You flagged EU data residency for EU customers; primary question: will EU user traffic need to be processed and stored exclusively in EU region?
- As discussed, doing full EU residency (separate EU deployment) typically adds 10–25% to per-token unit costs because of reserved capacity sizing and smaller regional pools. We'll model both single-region (US multi-tenant) and dual-region (US + EU dedicated) scenarios.

Next steps (agreed)
1) I’ll send a detailed pricing workbook (attached) with three scenarios: Hosted US-only, Hosted EU-only (if they require), and Dedicated (reserved capacity) TCO for mid/peak month.
2) We’ll include a line for ingress/egress and replication overhead for EU residency.
3) You’ll confirm whether EU traffic must remain in EU (yes/no) and the expected user split (approx % EU vs US).
4) Tentatively schedule a follow-up next Wed to review the workbook — I’ll send calendar invite once I know who from your infra/security team will join.

Attachments: pricing_workbook_finlytics_v1.xlsx (workbook contains token model + unit prices; initial default assumes US hosted pricing).

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa and Aditya internally for pricing verification.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: token volumes, budget range, next steps

Thanks for confirming, Alicia — appreciated. Short answers up front and next-week agenda draft below.

Ballpark EU uplift: Hosted EU vs Hosted US
- For the hosted (multi-tenant) product: expect ~12–18% uplift on unit $/1M tokens for EU-only processing due to regional infra costs and smaller amortization across customers. Example: if US hosted = $12/1M, EU hosted ≈ $13.40–$14.20/1M.

Dedicated (reserved capacity) delta
- Dedicated pools reduce per-token costs at scale because of reserved GPU efficiency, but they require an N-month commitment and have baseline monthly fees (in your case estimated: $40k–$55k/mo baseline for a minimal EU pool to meet latency SLOs). Net per-1M price could be 10–30% lower than hosted at high volumes, but only once you pass a threshold (we’ll show break-even in the workbook).

Quick wins to reduce unit cost while keeping latency
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts: can reduce token spend by 15–40% depending on prompt reuse.
- Dynamic batching during off-peak windows and adaptive concurrency to increase GPU utilization with minimal latency impact for non-interactive workloads.
- Model tiering: route shorter or lower-risk requests to smaller/cheaper model variants and reserve larger models for complex queries.

Proposed agenda for next Wed
- Walk through pricing_workbook: US-hosted vs EU-hosted vs Dedicated (break-even scenarios)
- Discuss data residency architecture and SLO tradeoffs (replication, retention, audit logs)
- Procurement redlines and sample contract terms (credits, SLAs)

I’ve attached a quick TCO estimate and SOC2 snapshot we promised. I’ll send a calendar invite with a proposed time and include a readout tab in the workbook that highlights the per-1M cost at three volume points: 50M, 250M, 1B tokens/month.

Attachments: redwood_tco_estimate.pdf, soc2-snapshot-2025.zip, pricing_workbook_finlytics_v1.xlsx (updated).

Thanks — I’ll propose Wed 17:00 CET / 9:00 PST; let me know if that collides with Ellen/Marcus.

Best,
Jordan
